newsitem.title: UK: London to be Europe centre regardless of EMU-LIFFE.
newsitem.headline: London to be Europe centre regardless of EMU-LIFFE.

text.p: London will remain the main financial centre for Europe regardless of Britain's position on monetary union, said Daniel Hodson, chief executive of London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) on Thursday.

Speaking at a conference on EMU, Hodson said a successful derivatives market required a strong underlying cash market which London, as the largest European financial centre was well placed to provide.
"We are now recognised even by the Germans as the European money market," Hodson said.

This followed the Deutsche Boerse decision to change the configuration of its money market instruments from one based on Frankfurt interest rates to London interest rates, he said, and meant the euro money market interest rate would be set from London Interbank Offered Rates.
After 1999 Hodson said there would be a transitional period with a reserve fund provided by the European Central Bank, and it might be to London's advantage to be outside EMU.

"It could mean that London will be a purer money market, more accurate and more attractive to money market investors outside," he said. "This postulates that London, if it were offshore, may be at least as sucessful as if it were part of the union."
Hodson said LIFFE was well placed to trade the euro denominated bonds as it already traded 70 percent of the Bund contract, which was likely to be the dominant component of euro denominated bonds.
